auditNotes: Commit f62b23e removed plans/, docs/evidence, apps/windows/tools, crates/super-duper-core/examples, ROADMAP.md, several docs and 32 scripts. README.md, AGENTS.md, crates/CLAUDE.md and seven docs still referenced removed material.
No end-user documentation of the Windows app existed beyond README and CHANGELOG bullets; no maintainer architecture documentation of the WPF app existed beyond AGENTS.md layering rules.
docs/architecture.svg predates the worker and shows the Windows app as a future FFI client. It is wrong and is removed; the replacement is a diagram request on arch-overview.
dev-notes.md duplicates AGENTS.md (storage) and README (runtime files) and is folded into those and removed, per #22.

House style: the repository wraps prose near 100 columns with several sentences per line and uses sentence-case headings in newer docs. Drafts follow the repository convention rather than docs-helper's one-sentence-per-line rule; every other docs-helper rule applies.
provenance.drafting: Phase 6 drafted 2026-09-19 on branch docs/windows-front-end. Prose follows the repository conventions noted in auditNotes. No diagrams were rendered (Node.js unavailable).

project.name: Super Duper
project.summary: Review-only duplicate file finder: a Rust engine and JSONL worker behind a WPF/.NET 10 Windows 11 app, plus a headless CLI and a C ABI.

audiences.name: Windows app user
audiences.description: Someone who downloads the release zip and uses the app to find duplicates and record keep/remove decisions. Knows Windows and their own folders; does not read code.

audiences.name: Maintainer
audiences.description: A developer or coding agent changing the Windows app, the worker or the engine. Reads C# and Rust; needs the layering, runtime behavior, conventions and decisions.

audiences.name: Release operator
audiences.description: The person who verifies and publishes a release on the dedicated Windows VM and runs the gates CI cannot.

sources.note: Composition root: .uidev sidecar (Debug), state locations, single-instance gate, DI registrations including DisabledRecycleOperationCapabilityExecutor, startup and exit.
Shell layout: tabs and sub-tabs, banners, recovery card, unsaved-setup prompt, responsive breakpoints, preference persistence, focus targets, shutdown sequence.
Every user-visible label, access key, keyboard handler and layout breakpoint.
AutomationNotificationBehavior, WindowTextScale, ShellResources tokens, WPF services (dialogs, clipboard, dispatcher), PlainPathConverter, ServerSortInteraction, DecisionActionFocus.
Navigation model (WorkspaceArea/Destination), pane loading, connection states, restart and recovery, completion navigation, close confirmation.
Behavior behind each screen: setup, progress, files, folders, preflight, preference rules, history, warnings, performance, recycle/recovery review.
Saved-scan validation rules, limits, default ignore patterns, drive-type warnings.
IWorkerClient families, DTOs, progress contract, WorkerDatabaseUnavailableException reasons and user text.
Process launch, hello handshake, correlation, event dispatch, stderr capture and log rotation, restart, live-hint batching.
Worker discovery rules (Debug vs Release), state folder and env overrides, single instance per state folder.
Explorer reveal and grouped selection, cloud sync-root detection, presentation preferences, Recycle Bin navigation, disabled vs real recycle executor.
Target frameworks, packages, version, worker copy targets, long-path manifest, CsWin32 APIs.
Workspace version, Rust floor, .NET SDK pin, license policy for notices.
View-model and validation behavior against in-memory doubles; the most reliable statement of intended UI behavior.
Protocol, locator, state, preferences, Explorer, real-worker lifecycle, database_unavailable, recovery; opt-in RealCloudProvider/RealRecycleBin/RealRecycleBinProvider categories.
In-process STA WPF surface tests with fixtures and optional capture variables.
Worker protocol smoke plus real-desktop WPF UI Automation journey and close scenarios.
Disposable-state Debug/Release launch, five-file fixture, .uidev control launch.
Release matrix, publish, notices, package; icon generation.
build-and-test and release-package jobs on windows-latest.
Method dispatch, events, error codes, database lock and database_unavailable, shutdown, progress projection.
Schema v15, migrations, open-failure classification, session delete cascade and refusal.
Status database schema and limits, progress constants and wire names.
Scan pipeline: discovery, size grouping, partial and full hashing, repeat cache, exact folders.
Claims audited against code; findings recorded per document.
What the cleanup removed and the owner's docs-refresh checklist.
Fixed MVP decisions (worker process not FFI, WPF Fluent, worker-only database access) and the redesign's alternatives and product invariants.
Why state moved to %LOCALAPPDATA%, why one owner per database, why Release launches only the sibling worker.
The earlier in-process FFI client and its handle-leak and dispose-race fixes.
Released features, requirements, SmartScreen note, known limitations for v0.1.0.

gaps.note: Nothing in this plan was observed in a running app. All UI behavior comes from XAML, view models and tests. A walkthrough of the user guide on the dedicated Windows VM is needed before the guide is called verified.

Access keys: tooltips on the next/previous duplicate-set buttons promise Alt+N/Alt+P but no binding exists (DuplicateFilesView.xaml:741-755, .xaml.cs:31). Progress announces Alt+W for Review warnings but its access key is R, already used by the Results and Review tabs (ScanProgressView.xaml:70-71). Alt+P on Progress is shared by the Progress tab and Performance details; Alt+F by the Files tab and Filters; Alt+R and Alt+S by top-level tabs; History shares R, N and P with its warnings controls. None of these are documented as working shortcuts; all keys are unverified at runtime.
The watcher notice tells users to 'choose Validate page' (DuplicateFilesViewModel.cs:1154) but the button is 'Check these copies'. Docs use the button label.
The header 'Scan again' button starts a scan immediately; ScanAgainCommand (open Setup) exists but is not bound. Whether that is intended is unknown; docs describe the current behavior.
The Repeat scans choice is not saved with the saved scan and resets to 'Reuse verified hashes' when a saved scan loads. Intent unknown; docs describe current behavior.
Unverified whether deleting a saved scan removes its telemetry from scan_status.db; docs do not claim either way.

The original rationale for a worker process over in-process FFI was never written down. ADR-0001 states the decision and verified consequences and cites the earlier WinUI 3/FFI client only as history.
Per-monitor DPI behavior without a dpiAwareness manifest entry, Fluent theme behavior under high contrast, and screen-reader behavior are unverified (issue #23).
Diagrams were not rendered: Node.js is not installed, so diagram-generator's renderer cannot run. The diagrams[] requests remain for a later pass; affected pages use text tables.
Field-by-field agreement between every C# DTO and each protocol JSON example was only spot-checked.
Whether the worker itself writes a diagnostic log at SUPER_DUPER_DIAGNOSTIC_LOG_PATH or only reports it as metadata was not traced; docs describe the app-side worker.log only.

Tooling decisions left to the owner: whether the protocol smoke should run the published worker, whether the build should fail when the worker is missing, and aligning Smoke.Tests to MSTest 4 (#35). Docs describe current behavior.

Worker log location: the app always writes worker stderr to %LOCALAPPDATA%\SuperDuper\logs, even with SUPER_DUPER_DB_PATH set (WorkerClient.cs:87, 1569), so smoke and UI-dev runs write into the real log folder despite the disposable-state rule. LOG_FILE_PATH set by Start-WindowsUiDev.ps1 and .uidev is read only by the CLI.

Code comment and output drift outside the docs: ci.yml:69-72 says release-package smokes the worker against the published app (it runs target/release); Invoke-WindowsSmoke.ps1:1717 still prints 1 GB-or-larger for the 1 GiB filter.

SessionDefinitionValidator calls Directory.Exists and DriveInfo on the UI thread for local and removable roots (SessionDefinitionValidator.cs:67,126,190), an exception to the no-filesystem-on-dispatcher rule. WorkerClient.DispatchEvent runs subscribers inside its error handling, so a handler exception kills the worker. DuplicateFoldersViewModel matches worker error codes by message text.
The release failure-mode pass (corrupt/newer/read-only database, worker kill, locked cache, missing and offline roots, long paths) has no written procedure; the checklist lists the cases only.

User-facing text still uses protocol terms in places: validation messages say session, and Cancel preflight and exit? and a Run preflight again announcement say preflight, while the rest of the UI says saved scan and Check marked copies.
